    53→class Query:
    54→    """Handles bidirectional control protocol on top of Transport.
    55→
    56→    This class manages:
    57→    - Control request/response routing
    58→    - Hook callbacks
    59→    - Tool permission callbacks
    60→    - Message streaming
    61→    - Initialization handshake
    62→    """
    63→
    64→    def __init__(
    65→        self,
    66→        transport: Transport,
    67→        is_streaming_mode: bool,
    68→        can_use_tool: Callable[
    69→            [str, dict[str, Any], ToolPermissionContext],
    70→            Awaitable[PermissionResultAllow | PermissionResultDeny],
    71→        ]
    72→        | None = None,
    73→        hooks: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None = None,
    74→        sdk_mcp_servers: dict[str, "McpServer"] | None = None,
    75→        initialize_timeout: float = 60.0,
    76→        agents: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    77→    ):
    78→        """Initialize Query with transport and callbacks.
    79→
    80→        Args:
    81→            transport: Low-level transport for I/O
    82→            is_streaming_mode: Whether using streaming (bidirectional) mode
    83→            can_use_tool: Optional callback for tool permission requests
    84→            hooks: Optional hook configurations
    85→            sdk_mcp_servers: Optional SDK MCP server instances
    86→            initialize_timeout: Timeout in seconds for the initialize request
    87→            agents: Optional agent definitions to send via initialize
    88→        """
    89→        self._initialize_timeout = initialize_timeout
    90→        self.transport = transport
    91→        self.is_streaming_mode = is_streaming_mode
    92→        self.can_use_tool = can_use_tool
    93→        self.hooks = hooks or {}
    94→        self.sdk_mcp_servers = sdk_mcp_servers or {}
    95→        self._agents = agents
    96→
    97→        # Control protocol state
    98→        self.pending_control_responses: dict[str, anyio.Event] = {}
    99→        self.pending_control_results: dict[str, dict[str, Any] | Exception] = {}
   100→        self.hook_callbacks: dict[str, Callable[..., Any]] = {}
   101→        self.next_callback_id = 0
   102→        self._request_counter = 0
   103→
   104→        # Message stream
   105→        self._message_send, self._message_receive = anyio.create_memory_object_stream[
   106→            dict[str, Any]
   107→        ](max_buffer_size=100)
   108→        self._tg: anyio.abc.TaskGroup | None = None
   109→        self._initialized = False
   110→        self._closed = False
   111→        self._initialization_result: dict[str, Any] | None = None
   112→
   113→        # Track first result for proper stream closure with SDK MCP servers
   114→        self._first_result_event = anyio.Event()
   115→        self._stream_close_timeout = (
   116→            float(os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT", "60000")) / 1000.0
   117→        )  # Convert ms to seconds
   118→
   119→    async def initialize(self) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
   120→        """Initialize control protocol if in streaming mode.
   121→
   122→        Returns:
   123→            Initialize response with supported commands, or None if not streaming
   124→        """
   125→        if not self.is_streaming_mode:
   126→            return None
   127→
   128→        # Build hooks configuration for initialization
   129→        hooks_config: dict[str, Any] = {}
   130→        if self.hooks:
   131→            for event, matchers in self.hooks.items():
   132→                if matchers:
   133→                    hooks_config[event] = []
   134→                    for matcher in matchers:
   135→                        callback_ids = []
   136→                        for callback in matcher.get("hooks", []):
   137→                            callback_id = f"hook_{self.next_callback_id}"
   138→                            self.next_callback_id += 1
   139→                            self.hook_callbacks[callback_id] = callback
   140→                            callback_ids.append(callback_id)
   141→                        hook_matcher_config: dict[str, Any] = {
   142→                            "matcher": matcher.get("matcher"),
   143→                            "hookCallbackIds": callback_ids,
   144→                        }
   145→                        if matcher.get("timeout") is not None:
   146→                            hook_matcher_config["timeout"] = matcher.get("timeout")
   147→                        hooks_config[event].append(hook_matcher_config)
   148→
   149→        # Send initialize request
   150→        request: dict[str, Any] = {
   151→            "subtype": "initialize",
   152→            "hooks": hooks_config if hooks_config else None,
   153→        }
   154→        if self._agents:
   155→            request["agents"] = self._agents
   156→
   157→        # Use longer timeout for initialize since MCP servers may take time to start
   158→        response = await self._send_control_request(
   159→            request, timeout=self._initialize_timeout
   160→        )
   161→        self._initialized = True
   162→        self._initialization_result = response  # Store for later access
   163→        return response
   164→
   165→    async def start(self) -> None:
   166→        """Start reading messages from transport."""
   167→        if self._tg is None:
   168→            self._tg = anyio.create_task_group()
   169→            await self._tg.__aenter__()
   170→            self._tg.start_soon(self._read_messages)
   171→
   172→    async def _read_messages(self) -> None:
   173→        """Read messages from transport and route them."""
   174→        try:
   175→            async for message in self.transport.read_messages():
   176→                if self._closed:
   177→                    break
   178→
   179→                msg_type = message.get("type")
   180→
   181→                # Route control messages
   182→                if msg_type == "control_response":
   183→                    response = message.get("response", {})
   184→                    request_id = response.get("request_id")
   185→                    if request_id in self.pending_control_responses:
   186→                        event = self.pending_control_responses[request_id]
   187→                        if response.get("subtype") == "error":
   188→                            self.pending_control_results[request_id] = Exception(
   189→                                response.get("error", "Unknown error")
   190→                            )
   191→                        else:
   192→                            self.pending_control_results[request_id] = response
   193→                        event.set()
   194→                    continue
   195→
   196→                elif msg_type == "control_request":
   197→                    # Handle incoming control requests from CLI
   198→                    # Cast message to SDKControlRequest for type safety
   199→                    request: SDKControlRequest = message  # type: ignore[assignment]
   200→                    if self._tg:
   201→                        self._tg.start_soon(self._handle_control_request, request)
   202→                    continue
   203→
   204→                elif msg_type == "control_cancel_request":
   205→                    # Handle cancel requests
   206→                    # TODO: Implement cancellation support
   207→                    continue
   208→
   209→                # Track results for proper stream closure
   210→                if msg_type == "result":
   211→                    self._first_result_event.set()
   212→
   213→                # Regular SDK messages go to the stream
   214→                await self._message_send.send(message)
   215→
   216→        except anyio.get_cancelled_exc_class():
   217→            # Task was cancelled - this is expected behavior
   218→            logger.debug("Read task cancelled")
   219→            raise  # Re-raise to properly handle cancellation
   220→        except Exception as e:
   221→            logger.error(f"Fatal error in message reader: {e}")
   222→            # Signal all pending control requests so they fail fast instead of timing out
   223→            for request_id, event in list(self.pending_control_responses.items()):
   224→                if request_id not in self.pending_control_results:
   225→                    self.pending_control_results[request_id] = e
   226→                    event.set()
   227→            # Put error in stream so iterators can handle it
   228→            await self._message_send.send({"type": "error", "error": str(e)})
   229→        finally:
   230→            # Always signal end of stream
   231→            await self._message_send.send({"type": "end"})
   232→
   233→    async def _handle_control_request(self, request: SDKControlRequest) -> None:
   234→        """Handle incoming control request from CLI."""
   235→        request_id = request["request_id"]
   236→        request_data = request["request"]
   237→        subtype = request_data["subtype"]
   238→
   239→        try:
   240→            response_data: dict[str, Any] = {}
   241→
   242→            if subtype == "can_use_tool":
   243→                permission_request: SDKControlPermissionRequest = request_data  # type: ignore[assignment]
   244→                original_input = permission_request["input"]
   245→                # Handle tool permission request
   246→                if not self.can_use_tool:
   247→                    raise Exception("canUseTool callback is not provided")
   248→
   249→                context = ToolPermissionContext(
   250→                    signal=None,  # TODO: Add abort signal support
   251→                    suggestions=permission_request.get("permission_suggestions", [])
   252→                    or [],
   253→                )
   254→
   255→                response = await self.can_use_tool(
   256→                    permission_request["tool_name"],
   257→                    permission_request["input"],
   258→                    context,
   259→                )
   260→
   261→                # Convert PermissionResult to expected dict format
   262→                if isinstance(response, PermissionResultAllow):
   263→                    response_data = {
   264→                        "behavior": "allow",
   265→                        "updatedInput": (
   266→                            response.updated_input
   267→                            if response.updated_input is not None
   268→                            else original_input
   269→                        ),
   270→                    }
   271→                    if response.updated_permissions is not None:
   272→                        response_data["updatedPermissions"] = [
   273→                            permission.to_dict()
   274→                            for permission in response.updated_permissions
   275→                        ]
   276→                elif isinstance(response, PermissionResultDeny):
   277→                    response_data = {"behavior": "deny", "message": response.message}
   278→                    if response.interrupt:
   279→                        response_data["interrupt"] = response.interrupt
   280→                else:
   281→                    raise TypeError(
   282→                        f"Tool permission callback must return PermissionResult (PermissionResultAllow or PermissionResultDeny), got {type(response)}"
   283→                    )
   284→
   285→            elif subtype == "hook_callback":
   286→                hook_callback_request: SDKHookCallbackRequest = request_data  # type: ignore[assignment]
   287→                # Handle hook callback
   288→                callback_id = hook_callback_request["callback_id"]
   289→                callback = self.hook_callbacks.get(callback_id)
   290→                if not callback:
   291→                    raise Exception(f"No hook callback found for ID: {callback_id}")
   292→
   293→                hook_output = await callback(
   294→                    request_data.get("input"),
   295→                    request_data.get("tool_use_id"),
   296→                    {"signal": None},  # TODO: Add abort signal support
   297→                )
   298→                # Convert Python-safe field names (async_, continue_) to CLI-expected names (async, continue)
   299→                response_data = _convert_hook_output_for_cli(hook_output)
   300→
   301→            elif subtype == "mcp_message":
   302→                # Handle SDK MCP request
   303→                server_name = request_data.get("server_name")
   304→                mcp_message = request_data.get("message")
   305→
   306→                if not server_name or not mcp_message:
   307→                    raise Exception("Missing server_name or message for MCP request")
   308→
   309→                # Type narrowing - we've verified these are not None above
   310→                assert isinstance(server_name, str)
   311→                assert isinstance(mcp_message, dict)
   312→                mcp_response = await self._handle_sdk_mcp_request(
   313→                    server_name, mcp_message
   314→                )
   315→                # Wrap the MCP response as expected by the control protocol
   316→                response_data = {"mcp_response": mcp_response}
   317→
   318→            else:
   319→                raise Exception(f"Unsupported control request subtype: {subtype}")
   320→
   321→            # Send success response
   322→            success_response: SDKControlResponse = {
   323→                "type": "control_response",
   324→                "response": {
   325→                    "subtype": "success",
   326→                    "request_id": request_id,
   327→                    "response": response_data,
   328→                },
   329→            }
   330→            await self.transport.write(json.dumps(success_response) + "\n")
   331→
   332→        except Exception as e:
   333→            # Send error response
   334→            error_response: SDKControlResponse = {
   335→                "type": "control_response",
   336→                "response": {
   337→                    "subtype": "error",
   338→                    "request_id": request_id,
   339→                    "error": str(e),
   340→                },
   341→            }
   342→            await self.transport.write(json.dumps(error_response) + "\n")
   343→
   344→    async def _send_control_request(
   345→        self, request: dict[str, Any], timeout: float = 60.0
   346→    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
   347→        """Send control request to CLI and wait for response.
   348→
   349→        Args:
   350→            request: The control request to send
   351→            timeout: Timeout in seconds to wait for response (default 60s)
   352→        """
   353→        if not self.is_streaming_mode:
   354→            raise Exception("Control requests require streaming mode")
   355→
   356→        # Generate unique request ID
   357→        self._request_counter += 1
   358→        request_id = f"req_{self._request_counter}_{os.urandom(4).hex()}"
   359→
   360→        # Create event for response
   361→        event = anyio.Event()
   362→        self.pending_control_responses[request_id] = event
   363→
   364→        # Build and send request
   365→        control_request = {
   366→            "type": "control_request",
   367→            "request_id": request_id,
   368→            "request": request,
   369→        }
   370→
   371→        await self.transport.write(json.dumps(control_request) + "\n")
   372→
   373→        # Wait for response
   374→        try:
   375→            with anyio.fail_after(timeout):
   376→                await event.wait()
   377→
   378→            result = self.pending_control_results.pop(request_id)
   379→            self.pending_control_responses.pop(request_id, None)
   380→
   381→            if isinstance(result, Exception):
   382→                raise result
   383→
   384→            response_data = result.get("response", {})
   385→            return response_data if isinstance(response_data, dict) else {}
   386→        except TimeoutError as e:
   387→            self.pending_control_responses.pop(request_id, None)
   388→            self.pending_control_results.pop(request_id, None)
   389→            raise Exception(f"Control request timeout: {request.get('subtype')}") from e
   390→
   391→    async def _handle_sdk_mcp_request(
   392→        self, server_name: str, message: dict[str, Any]
   393→    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
   394→        """Handle an MCP request for an SDK server.
   395→
   396→        This acts as a bridge between JSONRPC messages from the CLI
   397→        and the in-process MCP server. Ideally the MCP SDK would provide
   398→        a method to handle raw JSONRPC, but for now we route manually.
   399→
   400→        Args:
   401→            server_name: Name of the SDK MCP server
   402→            message: The JSONRPC message
   403→
   404→        Returns:
   405→            The response message
   406→        """
   407→        if server_name not in self.sdk_mcp_servers:
   408→            return {
   409→                "jsonrpc": "2.0",
   410→                "id": message.get("id"),
   411→                "error": {
   412→                    "code": -32601,
   413→                    "message": f"Server '{server_name}' not found",
   414→                },
   415→            }
   416→
   417→        server = self.sdk_mcp_servers[server_name]
   418→        method = message.get("method")
   419→        params = message.get("params", {})
   420→
   421→        try:
   422→            # TODO: Python MCP SDK lacks the Transport abstraction that TypeScript has.
   423→            # TypeScript: server.connect(transport) allows custom transports
   424→            # Python: server.run(read_stream, write_stream) requires actual streams
   425→            #
   426→            # This forces us to manually route methods. When Python MCP adds Transport
   427→            # support, we can refactor to match the TypeScript approach.
   428→            if method == "initialize":
   429→                # Handle MCP initialization - hardcoded for tools only, no listChanged
   430→                return {
   431→                    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
   432→                    "id": message.get("id"),
   433→                    "result": {
   434→                        "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05",
   435→                        "capabilities": {
   436→                            "tools": {}  # Tools capability without listChanged
   437→                        },
   438→                        "serverInfo": {
   439→                            "name": server.name,
   440→                            "version": server.version or "1.0.0",
   441→                        },
   442→                    },
   443→                }
   444→
   445→            elif method == "tools/list":
   446→                request = ListToolsRequest(method=method)
   447→                handler = server.request_handlers.get(ListToolsRequest)
   448→                if handler:
   449→                    result = await handler(request)
   450→                    # Convert MCP result to JSONRPC response
   451→                    tools_data = []
   452→                    for tool in result.root.tools:  # type: ignore[union-attr]
   453→                        tool_data: dict[str, Any] = {
   454→                            "name": tool.name,
   455→                            "description": tool.description,
   456→                            "inputSchema": (
   457→                                tool.inputSchema.model_dump()
   458→                                if hasattr(tool.inputSchema, "model_dump")
   459→                                else tool.inputSchema
   460→                            )
   461→                            if tool.inputSchema
   462→                            else {},
   463→                        }
   464→                        if tool.annotations:
   465→                            tool_data["annotations"] = tool.annotations.model_dump(
   466→                                exclude_none=True
   467→                            )
   468→                        tools_data.append(tool_data)
   469→                    return {
   470→                        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
   471→                        "id": message.get("id"),
   472→                        "result": {"tools": tools_data},
   473→                    }
   474→
   475→            elif method == "tools/call":
   476→                call_request = CallToolRequest(
   477→                    method=method,
   478→                    params=CallToolRequestParams(
   479→                        name=params.get("name"), arguments=params.get("arguments", {})
   480→                    ),
   481→                )
   482→                handler = server.request_handlers.get(CallToolRequest)
   483→                if handler:
   484→                    result = await handler(call_request)
   485→                    # Convert MCP result to JSONRPC response
   486→                    content = []
   487→                    for item in result.root.content:  # type: ignore[union-attr]
   488→                        if hasattr(item, "text"):
   489→                            content.append({"type": "text", "text": item.text})
   490→                        elif hasattr(item, "data") and hasattr(item, "mimeType"):
   491→                            content.append(
   492→                                {
   493→                                    "type": "image",
   494→                                    "data": item.data,
   495→                                    "mimeType": item.mimeType,
   496→                                }
   497→                            )
   498→
   499→                    response_data = {"content": content}
   500→                    if hasattr(result.root, "is_error") and result.root.is_error:
   501→                        response_data["is_error"] = True  # type: ignore[assignment]
   502→
   503→                    return {
   504→                        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
   505→                        "id": message.get("id"),
   506→                        "result": response_data,
   507→                    }
   508→
   509→            elif method == "notifications/initialized":
   510→                # Handle initialized notification - just acknowledge it
   511→                return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {}}
   512→
   513→            # Add more methods here as MCP SDK adds them (resources, prompts, etc.)
   514→            # This is the limitation Ashwin pointed out - we have to manually update
   515→
   516→            return {
   517→                "jsonrpc": "2.0",
   518→                "id": message.get("id"),
   519→                "error": {"code": -32601, "message": f"Method '{method}' not found"},
   520→            }
   521→
   522→        except Exception as e:
   523→            return {
   524→                "jsonrpc": "2.0",
   525→                "id": message.get("id"),
   526→                "error": {"code": -32603, "message": str(e)},
   527→            }

   570→    async def stream_input(self, stream: AsyncIterable[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
   571→        """Stream input messages to transport.
   572→
   573→        If SDK MCP servers or hooks are present, waits for the first result
   574→        before closing stdin to allow bidirectional control protocol communication.
   575→        """
   576→        try:
   577→            async for message in stream:
   578→                if self._closed:
   579→                    break
   580→                await self.transport.write(json.dumps(message) + "\n")
   581→
   582→            # If we have SDK MCP servers or hooks that need bidirectional communication,
   583→            # wait for first result before closing the channel
   584→            has_hooks = bool(self.hooks)
   585→            if self.sdk_mcp_servers or has_hooks:
   586→                logger.debug(
   587→                    f"Waiting for first result before closing stdin "
   588→                    f"(sdk_mcp_servers={len(self.sdk_mcp_servers)}, has_hooks={has_hooks})"
   589→                )
   590→                try:
   591→                    with anyio.move_on_after(self._stream_close_timeout):
   592→                        await self._first_result_event.wait()
   593→                        logger.debug("Received first result, closing input stream")
   594→                except Exception:
   595→                    logger.debug(
   596→                        "Timed out waiting for first result, closing input stream"
   597→                    )
   598→
   599→            # After all messages sent (and result received if needed), end input
   600→            await self.transport.end_input()
   601→        except Exception as e:
   602→            logger.debug(f"Error streaming input: {e}")
   603→
   604→    async def receive_messages(self) -> AsyncIterator[dict[str, Any]]:
   605→        """Receive SDK messages (not control messages)."""
   606→        async for message in self._message_receive:
   607→            # Check for special messages
   608→            if message.get("type") == "end":
   609→                break
   610→            elif message.get("type") == "error":
   611→                raise Exception(message.get("error", "Unknown error"))
   612→
   613→            yield message
   614→
   615→    async def close(self) -> None:
   616→        """Close the query and transport."""
   617→        self._closed = True
   618→        if self._tg:
   619→            self._tg.cancel_scope.cancel()

     4→from dataclasses import asdict, replace
     5→from typing import Any
     6→
     7→from ..types import (
     8→    ClaudeAgentOptions,
     9→    HookEvent,
    10→    HookMatcher,
    11→    Message,
    12→)
    13→from .message_parser import parse_message
    14→from .query import Query
    15→from .transport import Transport
    16→from .transport.subprocess_cli import SubprocessCLITransport
    17→

    19→class InternalClient:
    20→    """Internal client implementation."""
    21→
    22→    def __init__(self) -> None:
    23→        """Initialize the internal client."""
    24→
    25→    def _convert_hooks_to_internal_format(
    26→        self, hooks: dict[HookEvent, list[HookMatcher]]
    27→    ) -> dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    28→        """Convert HookMatcher format to internal Query format."""
    29→        internal_hooks: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
    30→        for event, matchers in hooks.items():
    31→            internal_hooks[event] = []
    32→            for matcher in matchers:
    33→                # Convert HookMatcher to internal dict format
    34→                internal_matcher: dict[str, Any] = {
    35→                    "matcher": matcher.matcher if hasattr(matcher, "matcher") else None,
    36→                    "hooks": matcher.hooks if hasattr(matcher, "hooks") else [],
    37→                }
    38→                if hasattr(matcher, "timeout") and matcher.timeout is not None:
    39→                    internal_matcher["timeout"] = matcher.timeout
    40→                internal_hooks[event].append(internal_matcher)
    41→        return internal_hooks
    42→
    43→    async def process_query(
    44→        self,
    45→        prompt: str | AsyncIterable[dict[str, Any]],
    46→        options: ClaudeAgentOptions,
    47→        transport: Transport | None = None,
    48→    ) -> AsyncIterator[Message]:
    49→        """Process a query through transport and Query."""
    50→
    51→        # Validate and configure permission settings (matching TypeScript SDK logic)
    52→        configured_options = options
    53→        if options.can_use_tool:
    54→            # canUseTool callback requires streaming mode (AsyncIterable prompt)
    55→            if isinstance(prompt, str):
    56→                raise ValueError(
    57→                    "can_use_tool callback requires streaming mode. "
    58→                    "Please provide prompt as an AsyncIterable instead of a string."
    59→                )
    60→
    61→            # canUseTool and permission_prompt_tool_name are mutually exclusive
    62→            if options.permission_prompt_tool_name:
    63→                raise ValueError(
    64→                    "can_use_tool callback cannot be used with permission_prompt_tool_name. "
    65→                    "Please use one or the other."
    66→                )
    67→
    68→            # Automatically set permission_prompt_tool_name to "stdio" for control protocol
    69→            configured_options = replace(options, permission_prompt_tool_name="stdio")
    70→
    71→        # Use provided transport or create subprocess transport
    72→        if transport is not None:
    73→            chosen_transport = transport
    74→        else:
    75→            chosen_transport = SubprocessCLITransport(
    76→                prompt=prompt,
    77→                options=configured_options,
    78→            )
    79→
    80→        # Connect transport
    81→        await chosen_transport.connect()
    82→
    83→        # Extract SDK MCP servers from configured options
    84→        sdk_mcp_servers = {}
    85→        if configured_options.mcp_servers and isinstance(
    86→            configured_options.mcp_servers, dict
    87→        ):
    88→            for name, config in configured_options.mcp_servers.items():
    89→                if isinstance(config, dict) and config.get("type") == "sdk":
    90→                    sdk_mcp_servers[name] = config["instance"]  # type: ignore[typeddict-item]
    91→
    92→        # Convert agents to dict format for initialize request
    93→        agents_dict = None
    94→        if configured_options.agents:
    95→            agents_dict = {
    96→                name: {k: v for k, v in asdict(agent_def).items() if v is not None}
    97→                for name, agent_def in configured_options.agents.items()
    98→            }
    99→
   100→        # Create Query to handle control protocol
   101→        # Always use streaming mode internally (matching TypeScript SDK)
   102→        # This ensures agents are always sent via initialize request
   103→        query = Query(
   104→            transport=chosen_transport,
   105→            is_streaming_mode=True,  # Always streaming internally
   106→            can_use_tool=configured_options.can_use_tool,
   107→            hooks=self._convert_hooks_to_internal_format(configured_options.hooks)
   108→            if configured_options.hooks
   109→            else None,
   110→            sdk_mcp_servers=sdk_mcp_servers,
   111→            agents=agents_dict,
   112→        )
   113→
   114→        try:
   115→            # Start reading messages
   116→            await query.start()
   117→
   118→            # Always initialize to send agents via stdin (matching TypeScript SDK)
   119→            await query.initialize()
   120→
   121→            # Handle prompt input
   122→            if isinstance(prompt, str):
   123→                # For string prompts, write user message to stdin after initialize
   124→                # (matching TypeScript SDK behavior)
   125→                import json
   126→
   127→                user_message = {
   128→                    "type": "user",
   129→                    "session_id": "",
   130→                    "message": {"role": "user", "content": prompt},
   131→                    "parent_tool_use_id": None,
   132→                }
   133→                await chosen_transport.write(json.dumps(user_message) + "\n")
   134→                await chosen_transport.end_input()
   135→            elif isinstance(prompt, AsyncIterable) and query._tg:
   136→                # Stream input in background for async iterables
   137→                query._tg.start_soon(query.stream_input, prompt)
   138→
   139→            # Yield parsed messages
   140→            async for data in query.receive_messages():
   141→                yield parse_message(data)
   142→
   143→        finally:
   144→            await query.close()

    40→            data,
    41→        )
    42→
    43→    message_type = data.get("type")
    44→    if not message_type:
    45→        raise MessageParseError("Message missing 'type' field", data)
    46→
    47→    match message_type:
    48→        case "user":
    49→            try:
    50→                parent_tool_use_id = data.get("parent_tool_use_id")
    51→                tool_use_result = data.get("tool_use_result")
    52→                uuid = data.get("uuid")
    53→                if isinstance(data["message"]["content"], list):
    54→                    user_content_blocks: list[ContentBlock] = []
    55→                    for block in data["message"]["content"]:
    56→                        match block["type"]:
    57→                            case "text":
    58→                                user_content_blocks.append(
    59→                                    TextBlock(text=block["text"])
    60→                                )
    61→                            case "tool_use":

    66→                                        input=block["input"],
    67→                                    )
    68→                                )
    69→                            case "tool_result":

   166→        case "stream_event":

1→"""Error types for Claude SDK."""
     2→
     3→from typing import Any
     4→
     5→
     6→class ClaudeSDKError(Exception):
     7→    """Base exception for all Claude SDK errors."""
     8→
     9→
    10→class CLIConnectionError(ClaudeSDKError):
    11→    """Raised when unable to connect to Claude Code."""
    12→
    13→
    14→class CLINotFoundError(CLIConnectionError):
    15→    """Raised when Claude Code is not found or not installed."""
    16→
    17→    def __init__(
    18→        self, message: str = "Claude Code not found", cli_path: str | None = None
    19→    ):
    20→        if cli_path:
    21→            message = f"{message}: {cli_path}"
    22→        super().__init__(message)
    23→
    24→
    25→class ProcessError(ClaudeSDKError):
    26→    """Raised when the CLI process fails."""
    27→
    28→    def __init__(
    29→        self, message: str, exit_code: int | None = None, stderr: str | None = None
    30→    ):
    31→        self.exit_code = exit_code
    32→        self.stderr = stderr
    33→
    34→        if exit_code is not None:
    35→            message = f"{message} (exit code: {exit_code})"
    36→        if stderr:
    37→            message = f"{message}\nError output: {stderr}"
    38→
    39→        super().__init__(message)
    40→
    41→
    42→class CLIJSONDecodeError(ClaudeSDKError):
    43→    """Raised when unable to decode JSON from CLI output."""
    44→
    45→    def __init__(self, line: str, original_error: Exception):
    46→        self.line = line
    47→        self.original_error = original_error
    48→        super().__init__(f"Failed to decode JSON: {line[:100]}...")
    49→
    50→
    51→class MessageParseError(ClaudeSDKError):
    52→    """Raised when unable to parse a message from CLI output."""
    53→
    54→    def __init__(self, message: str, data: dict[str, Any] | None = None):
    55→        self.data = data
    56→        super().__init__(message)

DEBUGGING "Fatal error in message reader" WHEN RESUMING TRUNCATED SESSION
===========================================================================

PROBLEM SUMMARY:
When trying to resume a truncated Claude Agent SDK session using the --resume flag,
the error "Fatal error in message reader" is logged and the operation fails.

================================================================================
1. WHERE THE ERROR COMES FROM
================================================================================

File: claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py
Line: 221
Code:
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Fatal error in message reader: {e}")

This is a catch-all exception handler in the Query._read_messages() method that
runs in an async background task. It catches ANY unhandled exception that occurs
while reading messages from the transport.

================================================================================
2. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS
================================================================================

The error chain is:

   SDK User Code
        ↓
   client.query(message, session_id=session_id)
        ↓
   InternalClient.process_query()
        ↓
   Query.start() + Query.receive_messages()
        ↓
   Query._read_messages() [background task] ← Exception handler is HERE
        ↓
   transport.read_messages()
        ↓
   SubprocessCLITransport._read_messages_impl()
        ↓
   [Waiting for subprocess output from Claude CLI]
        ↓
   CLI Process Exit with Non-Zero Code
        ↓
   ProcessError raised at line 585 of subprocess_cli.py
        ↓
   ProcessError caught by Query._read_messages() at line 220
        ↓
   Error logged: "Fatal error in message reader: <ProcessError>"

THE ACTUAL PROBLEM (THE PROCESSerror):

When --resume is used with a truncated session JSONL file:

1. The subprocess_cli.py builds the CLI command with "--resume <session_id>"
   (Line 227-228)

2. The claude CLI process is launched and tries to load the session from:
   ~/.claude/projects/-Users-cyyeh-Desktop-duckdb-data-agent/<session_id>.jsonl

3. IF THE SESSION FILE IS TRUNCATED OR MALFORMED:
   - The claude CLI fails to parse the session state
   - The CLI exits with a non-zero exit code (e.g., 1)
   - Before/after exit, it may write error messages to stderr
   - The CLI sends little to no output to stdout

4. The SDK's _read_messages_impl() detects the exit code != 0:
   
   File: subprocess_cli.py, Lines 572-585
   ```python
   # Check process completion and handle errors
   try:
       returncode = await self._process.wait()
   except Exception:
       returncode = -1

   # Use exit code for error detection
   if returncode is not None and returncode != 0:
       self._exit_error = ProcessError(
           f"Command failed with exit code {returncode}",
           exit_code=returncode,
           stderr="Check stderr output for details",
       )
       raise self._exit_error  ← This gets caught by Query._read_messages()
   ```

5. The ProcessError is caught and logged as "Fatal error in message reader"

================================================================================
3. HOW STDERR IS CAPTURED
================================================================================

The subprocess_cli.py HAS stderr capture capability (lines 360-388):

- stderr_dest = PIPE only if:
  a) self._options.stderr callback is provided, OR
  b) "debug-to-stderr" is in extra_args

- If stderr is piped, a background task (_handle_stderr) reads it:
  
  File: subprocess_cli.py, lines 412-438
  ```python
  async def _handle_stderr(self) -> None:
      # Reads stderr line by line and invokes callback
      if self._options.stderr:
          self._options.stderr(line_str)
  ```

- BUT by default in agent.py, NO stderr callback is configured!
  
  File: app/agent.py, lines 68-77
  ```python
  options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
      model=ANTHROPIC_MODEL,
      system_prompt=build_system_prompt(),
      mcp_servers={"duckdb": duckdb_server},
      allowed_tools=["mcp__duckdb__execute_sql"],
      permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
      max_turns=20,
      include_partial_messages=True,
      **({"resume": session_id} if session_id else {}),
  )  ← NO stderr= parameter!
  ```

CONSEQUENCE: When the CLI subprocess fails:
- stderr is NOT captured (stderr_dest=None at line 367)
- stderr is silently discarded
- The only error info is: "Command failed with exit code {returncode}"
- You get "Fatal error in message reader: Command failed with exit code 1"
  but NO DETAILS about WHY the CLI failed

================================================================================
4. SESSION DIRECTORY STRUCTURE
================================================================================

Location: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-cyyeh-Desktop-duckdb-data-agent/

Contents:
- <session-id>.jsonl files     [Main session records, JSONL format]
- <session-id>/ directories   [Session metadata + state]
  - subagents/                [Sub-agent session files]
  - tool-results/             [Tool execution results]
- memory/                      [Empty in this project]

The --resume flag looks for the .jsonl file with that session_id.

Session State in JSONL:
- Each line is a separate JSON object
- Types include: "user", "assistant", "progress", "system", "file-history-snapshot",
  "queue-operation", "stream_event"
- The file must be valid JSONL (one complete JSON object per line)

For the session f507e2f1-60b6-4deb-930d-1207c5ccdfab:
- Contains 1166 lines of valid JSON
- File size: 3.4MB
- Last modification: Feb 20 13:09:23 2026
- All lines are valid JSON (verified with Python json.loads())

================================================================================
5. SESSION RESUMPTION FLOW
================================================================================

When agent.py calls client.query() with session_id:

```python
# Line 76 in agent.py: Pass resume parameter
**({"resume": session_id} if session_id else {})

# This creates ClaudeAgentOptions with resume=<session_id>
```

The subprocess_cli.py processes it at line 227-228:
```python
if self._options.resume:
    cmd.extend(["--resume", self._options.resume])
```

The command becomes:
```
claude --output-format stream-json --verbose \
       --resume <session_id> \
       --input-format stream-json \
       [other options...]
```

The Claude CLI then:
1. Loads the session JSONL file by ID
2. Parses the previous conversation state
3. Sets up to continue from where it left off
4. Sends initialize request
5. Waits for new user input

IF THE SESSION FILE IS TRUNCATED:
- Step 1 fails (can't parse the truncated file)
- CLI exits with error code (non-zero)
- SDK detects exit code != 0
- Raises ProcessError
- Gets logged as "Fatal error in message reader"

================================================================================
6. KEY CODE LOCATIONS
================================================================================

Transport/Process Management:
- /claude_agent_sdk/_internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py
  - Lines 335-410: connect() - subprocess initialization
  - Lines 227-228: Resume flag handling in _build_command()
  - Lines 519-585: _read_messages_impl() - message reading and error detection

1→# DuckDB Data Agent
     2→
     3→> **Note:** This project is built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code)(using Opus 4.6 and [superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)) by more than 95% and human-reviewed by author.
     4→
     5→[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy)
     6→
     7→A SQL playground with an AI-powered data analysis agent. Upload CSV files, write SQL queries, or ask questions in plain English — powered by [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) on a lightweight [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend with a React frontend.
     8→
     9→## Features
    10→
    11→### SQL Playground
    12→
    13→- **DuckDB SQL engine** — Fast, in-process analytical database on the backend
    14→- **CSV file upload** — Drag-and-drop or click to import CSV files (up to 500 MB) with automatic schema detection
    15→- **Sample dataset** — One-click load of the Titanic dataset to get started quickly
    16→- **SQL query editor** — Write and execute queries with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
    17→- **Interactive results** — Sortable columns, per-column filters, and global search across results
    18→- **EXPLAIN support** — Markdown-rendered output for `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` queries
    19→- **Table sidebar** — Collapsible panel to browse tables, inspect columns, and view types
    20→
    21→### AI Agent
    22→
    23→- **Natural language queries** — Ask questions about your data in plain English; the agent writes and executes SQL for you
    24→- **Streaming responses** — Real-time token streaming powered by Claude via the [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
    25→- **Visible reasoning** — Collapsible thinking block shows the agent's intermediate steps and SQL queries
    26→- **Inline results** — Query results rendered inline within the conversation
    27→- **Privacy-conscious** — Requires an Anthropic API key stored in a server-side `.env` file; your data and key are never sent anywhere besides the Anthropic API
    28→- **Langfuse observability** (optional) — Built-in [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) tracing for monitoring agent interactions, with a one-click dashboard link in the UI
    29→
    30→## Getting Started
    31→
    32→### Prerequisites
    33→
    34→- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20+
    35→- [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.12+
    36→- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/)
    37→
    38→### Installation
    39→
    40→```bash
    41→make install
    42→```
    43→
    44→Or install frontend and backend separately:
    45→
    46→```bash
    47→cd frontend && npm install
    48→cd backend && poetry install
    49→```
    50→
    51→### Configuration
    52→
    53→Copy the example environment file and add your Anthropic API key:
    54→
    55→```bash
    56→cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
    57→```
    58→
    59→Edit `backend/.env` and set your key:
    60→
    61→```
    62→ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
    63→ANTHROPIC_MODEL=sonnet    # optional, defaults to sonnet
    64→```
    65→
    66→> Both variables are only needed for the AI agent. The SQL playground works without them, but both require the backend running.
    67→
    68→#### Langfuse (optional)
    69→
    70→To enable agent tracing with [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/), add these to `backend/.env`:
    71→
    72→```
    73→LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-...
    74→LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...
    75→LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com   # optional, defaults to cloud
    76→```
    77→
    78→When configured, every agent conversation is traced (LLM turns, tool calls, SQL execution) and a **Langfuse Traces** button appears in the agent panel header linking to your dashboard. When not configured, tracing is disabled with zero overhead.
    79→
    80→### Development
    81→
    82→Start both the frontend and backend:
    83→
    84→```bash
    85→make dev
    86→```
    87→
    88→Or run them separately:
    89→
    90→```bash
    91→make frontend   # http://localhost:5173
    92→make backend    # http://localhost:8000
    93→```
    94→
    95→Open http://localhost:5173 to use the app. The Vite dev server proxies `/api` requests to the backend automatically.
    96→
    97→## Production Build and Deployment
    98→
    99→The project ships as a single Docker image that bundles the React frontend and FastAPI backend. A multi-stage `Dockerfile` builds the frontend, then copies the output into the backend's static directory.
   100→
   101→### Build and run locally
   102→
   103→```bash
   104→docker build -t duckdb-data-agent .
   105→docker run -p 10000:10000 \
   106→  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... \
   107→  -e LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... \
   108→  -e LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... \
   109→  duckdb-data-agent
   110→```
   111→
   112→Open http://localhost:10000 to use the app.
   113→
   114→### Deploy to Render
   115→
   116→A `render.yaml` is included for one-click deployment on [Render](https://render.com/):
   117→
   118→1. Push this repo to GitHub.
   119→2. In Render, create a new **Blueprint** and connect the repo.
   120→3. Set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable in the Render dashboard. Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to override the default model (`sonnet`). To enable Langfuse tracing, also set `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`.
   121→
   122→Render will build the Docker image and deploy it automatically on every push to `main`.
   123→
   124→## Project Structure
   125→
   126→```
   127→├── frontend/               # React frontend
   128→│   ├── public/             #   Static assets (Langfuse icon)
   129→│   ├── src/
   130→│   │   ├── components/     #   UI components (editor, results, sidebar, chat)

# DuckDB Data Agent

> **Note:** This project is built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code)(using Opus 4.6 and [superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)) by more than 95% and human-reviewed by author.

[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy)

A SQL playground with an AI-powered data analysis agent. Upload CSV files, write SQL queries, or ask questions in plain English — powered by [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) on a lightweight [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend with a React frontend.

## Features

### SQL Playground

- **DuckDB SQL engine** — Fast, in-process analytical database on the backend
- **CSV file upload** — Drag-and-drop or click to import CSV files (up to 500 MB) with automatic schema detection
- **Sample dataset** — One-click load of the Titanic dataset to get started quickly
- **SQL query editor** — Write and execute queries with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
- **Interactive results** — Sortable columns, per-column filters, and global search across results
- **EXPLAIN support** — Markdown-rendered output for `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` queries
- **Table sidebar** — Collapsible panel to browse tables, inspect columns, and view types

### AI Agent

- **Natural language queries** — Ask questions about your data in plain English; the agent writes and executes SQL for you
- **Streaming responses** — Real-time token streaming powered by Claude via the [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
- **Visible reasoning** — Collapsible thinking block shows the agent's intermediate steps and SQL queries
- **Inline results** — Query results rendered inline within the conversation
- **Privacy-conscious** — Requires an Anthropic API key stored in a server-side `.env` file; your data and key are never sent anywhere besides the Anthropic API
- **Langfuse observability** (optional) — Built-in [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) tracing for monitoring agent interactions, with a one-click dashboard link in the UI

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20+
- [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.12+
- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/)

### Installation

```bash
make install
```

Or install frontend and backend separately:

```bash
cd frontend && npm install
cd backend && poetry install
```

### Configuration

Copy the example environment file and add your Anthropic API key:

```bash
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
```

Edit `backend/.env` and set your key:

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=sonnet    # optional, defaults to sonnet
```

> Both variables are only needed for the AI agent. The SQL playground works without them, but both require the backend running.

#### Langfuse (optional)

To enable agent tracing with [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/), add these to `backend/.env`:

```
LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-...
LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...
LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com   # optional, defaults to cloud
```

When configured, every agent conversation is traced (LLM turns, tool calls, SQL execution) and a **Langfuse Traces** button appears in the agent panel header linking to your dashboard. When not configured, tracing is disabled with zero overhead.

### Development

Start both the frontend and backend:

```bash
make dev
```

Or run them separately:

```bash
make frontend   # http://localhost:5173
make backend    # http://localhost:8000
```

Open http://localhost:5173 to use the app. The Vite dev server proxies `/api` requests to the backend automatically.

## Production Build and Deployment

The project ships as a single Docker image that bundles the React frontend and FastAPI backend. A multi-stage `Dockerfile` builds the frontend, then copies the output into the backend's static directory.

### Build and run locally

```bash
docker build -t duckdb-data-agent .
docker run -p 10000:10000 \
  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... \
  -e LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... \
  -e LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... \
  duckdb-data-agent
```

Open http://localhost:10000 to use the app.

### Deploy to Render

A `render.yaml` is included for one-click deployment on [Render](https://render.com/):

1. Push this repo to GitHub.
2. In Render, create a new **Blueprint** and connect the repo.
3. Set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable in the Render dashboard. Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to override the default model (`sonnet`). To enable Langfuse tracing, also set `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`.

Render will build the Docker image and deploy it automatically on every push to `main`.

## Project Structure

```
├── frontend/               # React frontend
│   ├── public/             #   Static assets (Langfuse icon)
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── components/     #   UI components (editor, results, sidebar, chat)
│   │   ├── agent/          #   Agent service (SSE event handling)
│   │   ├── AgentContext.tsx #   Agent state management
│   │   └── types.ts        #   Shared TypeScript interfaces
│   ├── index.html          #   HTML entry point
│   ├── package.json        #   npm config
│   └── vite.config.ts      #   Vite bundler config
├── backend/                # FastAPI backend
│   └── app/
│       ├── main.py         #   App setup & CORS
│       ├── config.py       #   Environment variables (API key, model)
│       ├── database.py     #   DuckDB connection & query execution
│       ├── agent.py        #   Agent loop & SSE streaming
│       ├── tracing.py      #   Langfuse client wrapper & initialization
│       ├── tools.py        #   Agent SDK tool definitions (execute_sql)
│       ├── data/           #   Sample datasets (titanic.csv)
│       └── routes/         #   API endpoints (tables, query, chat, langfuse status)
├── Dockerfile              # Multi-stage production build
├── render.yaml             # Render deployment config
└── Makefile                # Dev commands (install, dev, clean)
```

## Tech Stack

**Frontend**
- [React](https://react.dev/) 18 + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
- [Vite](https://vite.dev/)

**Backend**
- [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) + [Uvicorn](https://www.uvicorn.org/)
- [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) (Python)
- [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
- [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) (optional, for observability)

## License

[MIT](LICENSE.txt)
